curriculum.lesson_evidence: Trade connects Australia to the region and world through exports (goods sold out) and imports (goods bought in). Maps and simple flow diagrams show connections.

lesson.child_mission: Trade connects Australia to the region and world through exports (goods sold out) and imports (goods bought in). Maps and simple flow diagrams show connections.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Define export and import. Give one Australian example of each from a published list.

FEEDBACK
Export: sold to other countries; import: bought from other countries — examples per current published list.

WATCH FOR
Thinking trade only means shopping at a mall misses international flows.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Draw a trade connections map with four labelled flows from a published source. Write one sentence on why trade creates interdependence.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Trade connects Australia to the region and world through exports (goods sold out) and imports (goods bought in). Maps and simple flow diagrams show connections.
materials: Optional: local map, photo or interview notes
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Draw a trade connections map with four labelled flows from a published source. Write one sentence on why trade creates interdependence. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Export: sold to other countries; import: bought from other countries — examples per current published list. Reasoning: I used trade by attending to export rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Thinking trade only means shopping at a mall misses international flows. Correction: Export: sold to other countries; import: bought from other countries — examples per current published list. Why: the correction restores accurate use of trade.

Parent: Likely misconception: Thinking trade only means shopping at a mall misses international flows. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating trade on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with trade, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..

Trade connects Australia to the region and world through exports (goods sold out) and imports (goods bought in). Maps and simple flow diagrams show connections.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.
